title: Special levy adds nearly $400K to revenues - NewsBreak
text:
By none ,
11 hours ago Batesville’s regular sales tax diversion is not the only revenue source off to a strong start this fiscal year.
The city’s Tourism and Economic Development Tax generated an additional $200,430 in August, up from $172,071 during the same reporting period last year.
Through the first two months of the fiscal year, the special levy has returned $398,574 to Batesville, compared with $344,695 a year ago — an increase of $53,879, or 15.6 percent.
The special levy is separate from Batesville’s regular sales tax diversion and provides another measure of spending at businesses subject to the local tax.
Batesville’s collections also compare favorably with several other Mississippi municipalities.
Brandon received $183,535 from its special tax in August and $364,779 through the first two months of the fiscal year. Clinton received $176,327 in August and $348,652 year to date, while Cleveland reported $125,506 for August and $252,635 through two months.
Closer to Batesville, Senatobia’s special levy produced $63,435 in August and $133,299 through the first two months. Booneville received $51,514 in August and $99,350 year to date.
Those comparisons are not exact measures of the relative strength of the cities’ economies because special levies vary in their rates, purposes and the businesses to which they apply.
They do, however, provide perspective on the amount being generated by Batesville’s levy.
Like the regular sales tax diversion, special levy payments follow the Department of Revenue’s reporting cycle and do not necessarily represent purchases made during the month in which the payment is received.
